title: Fixed scheme of a correspondence
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and the coefficient conventions [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be the underlying geometric correspondence of a cohomological correspondence [def-trf-correspondence]. Write $a_X:X\to s$ for the structure morphism. Products here are fibre products of schemes [def-pc-fibre-product].

The diagonal $\Delta_X:X\to X\times_sX$ is the unique morphism whose composites with both projections are $\operatorname{id}_X$, that is, the morphism induced by the pair $(\operatorname{id}_X,\operatorname{id}_X)$.

The fixed scheme, with its two projections, is the fibre product
$$
F=\operatorname{Fix}(c):=C\times_{X\times_sX,c,\Delta_X}X,\qquad i_F:F\to C,\qquad d:F\to X.
$$
Thus the defining fibre-product relation is $c\circ i_F=\Delta_X\circ d$ and its two projection identities are $c_1\circ i_F=d=c_2\circ i_F$. This is the scheme-theoretic inverse image of the diagonal along $c$, as a scheme over $C$; the coefficient map of the cohomological correspondence is not used in this construction.

For an endomorphism $h:X\to X$ over $s$, meaning $a_X\circ h=a_X$, put
$$
\operatorname{Fix}(h):=X\times_{X\times_sX,(\operatorname{id}_X,h),\Delta_X}X.
$$
This is also denoted $\operatorname{Fix}((\operatorname{id}_X,h))$, using just the geometric correspondence. Its first projection is the scheme-theoretic equalizer of $h$ and $\operatorname{id}_X$: for every scheme $T$, a morphism $T\to\operatorname{Fix}(h)$ is uniquely specified by a morphism $t:T\to X$ with $h\circ t=t$.

A connected component of the underlying topological space of $F$ means a maximal nonempty connected subset, with connectedness in the subspace topology as in [def-weil-connected-scheme]; write $\pi_0(F)$ for the set of all these subsets. We say that $F$ has finitely many open-and-closed components when $\pi_0(F)$ is finite and every one of its members is open and closed in $F$. For such a component $\beta$, use the open subscheme structure
$$
\beta=(\beta,\mathcal O_F|_\beta)
$$
of [def-weil-open-immersion], without passing to a reduced subscheme. In this case the inclusions give the canonical identification
$$
\coprod_{\beta\in\pi_0(F)}\beta\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ F,
$$
where the coproduct is the scheme coproduct of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; morphisms from the disjoint open cover glue uniquely by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. The empty fixed scheme is allowed: its component set and its coproduct are both empty.
